subject: Re: Close date pressure — proposed traction recovery + escalation lane
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Javier Ortega <javier.ortega@acmehealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Close timeline risk — procurement hold expected next week

Michael —

Quick note from procurement: vendor verification hits a snag and their vendor approval meeting is pushed to 10/8. That effectively pushes our internal go/no-go beyond the 10/15 close we verbally committed to.

We still want to move forward with Redwood, but we need a concrete plan that:
- keeps core pilots live for our clinical-search evaluation
- gives procurement the artifacts they need in a single packet
- protects both parties from an illusory close date (we need a fallback cadence if procurement stretches)

Can you propose an alternative MAP or a staggered cutover approach we can present to the committee on Monday? Also attach any docs procurement will need (SOC2 evidence, retention policy, support SLA).

—Sarah
Sarah Lee
Director, Digital Strategy | Acme Health
[sent from mobile]

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Javier Ortega <javier.ortega@acmehealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close timeline risk — procurement hold expected next week

Sarah — thanks for the heads-up.

Short answer: yes. I put together a two-track MAP that preserves your evaluation objectives while acknowledging procurement's gating. Key points up-front:
- Staggered acceptance: pilot environment + limited token budget goes live on 10/15 (no formal MPA acceptance) so clinical teams can run evaluation scripts.
- Blocker gating: procurement receives one packet (SOC2 + retention + support commitment) by 10/4; if verification completes by 10/8 we proceed with formal MPA sign on 10/15.
- Escalation lane: if procurement misses 10/8, we commit to a “30/60” contingency with credits and a prioritized cutover window inside 30 days.

Attached: draft_map_v2.pdf (MAP showing staggered milestones) and procurement_timeline.xlsx (artifact checklist + owner/responsible).

If that matches what you need, I can loop in our CS and Legal to prepare the credit language and a short exec note for your committee.

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft_map_v2.pdf (6 pages)
Attachment: procurement_timeline.xlsx

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Close timeline risk — need quick buy-in on contingency credits + support SLA

Internal — forwarding Sarah's note plus my proposed MAP. Need quick input on two items before I reply to Acme: 
1) Credit construct: we propose 10% service credit on committed reserve if procurement delay >7 days. Approve/adjust?
2) Legal redlines: can we fast-track a one-page addendum that defines staggered acceptance (pilot-only launch + full acceptance on signed MPA)? Ben — can Legal produce a clean redline by COB Fri?

If we can't get legal, we should at least solidify the commercial ask to avoid losing momentum. Laura — can you confirm that our pilot infra team can stand up the restricted pilot (reduced throughput / token cap) on 10/15 regardless of formal MPA signature? Grace — heads-up for CS: if they go live early, we'll need a prioritized success queue for initial regressions.

Thanks — short replies please.

—Michael

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Close timeline risk — need quick buy-in on contingency credits + support SLA

Michael —

I can turn a one-page addendum around by COB tomorrow. Suggested guardrails:
- Staggered acceptance clause (pilot-only go-live)
- Conditional credit matrix (10% credit for >7d delay, 25% for >21d, cap at 50% of first month invoice)
- Limited SLA extension language (we keep production SLOs but open a prioritized triage for pilot tickets)

I'll draft and send as legal_redline.docx and copy you. For exec asks, I recommend we avoid fixed-dollar credits; percentage keeps it simple.

Ben
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Javier Ortega <javier.ortega@acmehealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2026 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close timeline risk — procurement hold expected next week

Michael — thanks, this is helpful. The staggered approach is promising and gives the evaluation team runway. A few asks from our committee:
- Procurement needs a single PDF packet for 10/4 (SOC2 + retention + support SLA + contact list).
- Legal would like the one-page addendum to include the credit matrix you mentioned. Priya will redline but is comfortable with percentage-based credits.
- Can we get formal language by COB 10/4 so I can circulate to the approval committee for a 10/5 vote?

If you can provide the packet and Ben's addendum draft tomorrow morning I can present it and push for the 10/5 vote. If committee greenlights, we'll aim to run the pilot on 10/15 as you proposed and proceed to formal MPA sign in the week that follows.

I'll accept the draft_map_v2.pdf as the basis for internal review.

—Sarah
Sarah Lee
Director, Digital Strategy | Acme Health
